A short finite intersection-cell triangulation argument supplies the desired refinement, but the cited statement alone is narrower than F2.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: 2.1 Apply [F2] to $T$ and $T_0$ to obtain a common finite linear refinement $T'$. It is a subdivision of $T$, and it refines every simplex of the subcomplex representing $f(P)$; therefore the simplices of $T'$ contained in $f(P)$ form a subcomplex by [F3], with realization exactly $f(P)$. required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: 2.1 Regard $T$ and $T_0$ as finite linear complexes on the same embedded polyhedron $Q$. Form all nonempty cells $\sigma\cap\tau$ for $\sigma\in T$ and $\tau\in T_0$, together with their faces. By [F2] these form a finite convex cell complex covering $Q$, and a compatible finite simplicial triangulation $T'$ of that cell complex exists. Each simplex of $T'$ lies in a cell contained in a simplex of $T$ and a simplex of $T_0$, so $T'$ is a common linear refinement. In particular it is a subdivision of $T$. Every simplex of the subcomplex representing $f(P)$ is a union of these refined simplices; thus the simplices of $T'$ contained in $f(P)$ have realization exactly $f(P)$ and form a subcomplex by [F3]. [given, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct] ∎
